Meeting header:
Date: 2027-06-11 | Start: 16:00 UTC | Duration: 48m
Attendees: Maya Patel (Redwood AE), Owen Reed (Redwood SE), Amir Khan (Suncrest CTO), Hana Li (Lead SRE), Jorge Morales (Product)

Auto-summary (auto-gen, may be incomplete):
- Demo of Console replay / correlator features focused on tracing request journeys, error clustering, and KV cache fallbacks.
- Discussed data residency and VPC/private deployment options.
- Agreed to run replay benchmarks and share security package.

Topics: replay playback, trace correlator, request logs, KV cache fallback, dedicated vs hosted inference, SOC2/KMS, pilot criteria

Transcript:
[00:00] Maya: Cool, uh, thanks everyone for joining, I, I think we've got about 45, 48 minutes, so we'll keep this tight. I'm Maya from Redwood, AE. Owen will run through the console walk-through and then we'll take questions. Amir, Hana, Jorge, thanks for making time.
[00:18] Amir: Hey thanks, Maya. Good to be here. Busy week so appreciate it.
[00:22] Owen: Yep hi all. I'm Owen, technical, gonna share my screen now. If you don't see it in a sec shout.
[00:30] [screen share noise / brief pause]
[00:35] Owen: Ok so first slide is a quick map, the replay correlator sits in the console under 'Request Inspector' — it stitches traces, request logs, and model responses into a single timeline. We built the correlator to make it easy to find the root cause span — like, whether it's a KV cache miss, a batching delay, or a model variant fallback.
[00:54] Hana: Sorry, can you repeat KV cache — you mean the prefix cache the runtime keeps in memory?
[00:58] Owen: Yeah the K-V cache, sometimes the transcription labels it 'K V cash' which is, uh, funny but, yes it's the prefix/kv cache. When there's a cache miss it shows as a fallback span and we highlight downstream latency impact.
[01:12] Amir: Do you get the actual tokens for the cache entries or is it just metadata?
[01:18] Owen: Great question. We surface metadata by default — key ids, hit/miss, and hash. For customers on private or dedicated we can show token-level deltas if you opt-in. Token visibility is gated for privacy and performance reasons, and there's an admin toggle.
[01:35] Jorge: How does that interact with encryption — we use a KMS and HSM currently.
[01:40] Maya: We integrate with your KMS for key management; on Private deployments the HSM/KMS trust boundary stays customer-managed. We'll include the security diagram in the pack.
[01:49] Owen: Back to the demo — here's a request timeline where a single user request crossed three services. Watch the correlator combine the traces and show error clustering on the left.
[02:05] [clicks]
[02:10] Owen: See here at t+1.2s there's a fallback to a smaller model variant — that's marked as 'model_fallback' and shows the pre- and post-token timing. You can click to open the response diff.
[02:22] Hana: Is that automatic? Like if capacity is low does Redwood auto-fallback by policy?
[02:27] Owen: Yep, we have routing policies — latency-first, cost-first, and regional-fallback. Ops teams can define canaries and auto-fallback thresholds. The trace will show which policy executed.
[02:38] Amir: Ok, on SLA side, what guarantees do you provide for dedicated pools? p95?
[02:43] Maya: Dedicated comes with SLA-backed latency targets and reserved throughput. We'll get you the SLA doc; typical p95 numbers depend on model and sequence length, we'll run the replay to show realistic numbers.
[02:54] Jorge: I want to see cost delta between using prefix cache aggressively vs disabled — do you show estimated token savings?
[02:59] Owen: We do. There's an Optimize panel that estimates token-level savings from prefix caching, batching, and quantization. In the replay mode we can project cost per 1M tokens based on your observed distribution.
[03:13] [background cough]
[03:16] Owen: Now showing the request inspector playback — you can scrub the timeline; at each timestamp we show service logs, request headers, and model response. Note: log parsing isn't perfect, sometimes field names differ based on customer's logging conventions.
[03:30] Hana: That was my next question — we use structured logs in JSON with nested context. Does the inspector flatten them or preserve structure?
[03:37] Owen: The console preserves the log payload and tries to surface primary fields. For extremely nested payloads it offers a raw view. The search index flattens key paths for fast lookup — occasionally you'll see key names mangled a bit in the auto-extracted fields.
[03:52] Amir: Data residency: if we run the console in private mode in our VPC does any data leave the VPC for the control plane?
[03:58] Maya: For Private, the control plane can be customer-hosted; nothing leaves your VPC unless you opt-in. We have an on-prem package for air-gapped environments, and we'll send the exact network diagram.
[04:10] Jorge: Sounds good. On the replay run — what throughput can you simulate? We have spikes to 5k rps during batch load windows.
[04:18] Owen: For hosted accounts we can simulate up to our burst thresholds; for dedicated we can replay at the target reserved throughput. In practice we run replays in a sandbox mode so they don't affect production. We'll test a sample at target qps and a full 24-hr replay to measure latency distribution and cache hit evolution.
[04:36] [15s pause as Owen switches views]
[04:52] Owen: Here's an error clustering view — you can group by exception message, by request path, or by model output pattern. For one customer we grouped by 'length mismatch' and discovered a prompt truncation earlier in the pipeline.
[05:05] Hana: Do you support attaching our internal incident IDs to traces? We want to cross-reference Sentry/Datadog.
[05:11] Owen: Yes, you can inject external IDs via a correlation header or in the request metadata. The correlator will pull it into the timeline and you can filter by external incident id.
[05:20] Amir: What about retention — how long are traces kept?
[05:24] Maya: Retention is configurable by plan — hosted default is 30 days; Extended retention is an add-on. For Private you control retention entirely. We'll include the retention table in the pack.
[05:34] Jorge: Any quota issues with the replay — i.e., does replay consume normal tokens and count against billing?
[05:40] Maya: Replays are billed as regular inference; for pilot work we usually grant a sandbox credit, we'll confirm in the pricing follow-up.
[05:48] Owen: Now jumping to a live example: a recent incident where a KV cache thrash caused p95 to spike. You can see repeated misses in a short window, the correlator highlights the cause and suggests a mitigation — increase cache TTL or enable warmed prefixes.
[06:05] Hana: Warmed prefixes, how would that work operationally?
[06:09] Owen: You can pre-populate the KV cache with frequent prefixes, or use an async warming job. In Dedicated you can also allocate a hot cache pool. The console will recommend warming candidates based on access frequency.
[06:20] [slight crosstalk]
[06:24] Jorge: Do you provide hooks for our SRE to run custom scripts on error clusters?
[06:28] Owen: There's an actions framework — you can wire Slack, webhook, or run a small lambda to extract context. For sensitive environments you can keep the actions inside VPC.
[06:38] Amir: On compliance — SOC2, ISO, and do you provide audit logs for admin activity?
[06:43] Maya: Yes, audit logs, RBAC, SSO via SAML/Okta are standard in enterprise packages. We'll attach the SOC2 summary and a sample audit log export.
[06:54] Hana: Would we be able to restrict access so only our SREs see token-level diffs?
[06:58] Owen: Absolutely — RBAC scopes token visibility to roles. By default token diffs are off for AE/Viewer roles.
[07:06] [longer pause as Owen runs a sandbox replay]
[07:40] Owen: Ok running the 24-hour replay now against a small sample — you can see the hit-rate heatmap on the right. Watch the cache warming at hour 2, then a sustained hit-rate of ~78%. When I toggle to a dedicated config, p95 drops by ~140ms in this sample.
[08:02] [cursor noise]
[08:08] Jorge: Is the delta mostly due to reduced batching latency or less serialization overhead?
[08:12] Owen: It's a mix — dedicated GPUs reduce queueing and also let us pick lower-latency kernels. Batching policies also differ; dedicated has more aggressive coalescing without impacting noisy neighbors.
[08:24] Amir: Could we see this with our own model variants? We have a proprietary seq2seq tuned model.
[08:29] Owen: Yes we can onboard model artifacts to the dedicated pool; we do a small compatibility pass and kernel selection. For private deployments you can also bring weights and we run the same runtime.
[08:40] Hana: About bring-your-own-model: any IP leakage risks during onboarding?
[08:44] Maya: We perform onboarding in an isolated build environment. If it's Private/on-prem the weights never leave your environment. We'll detail this process in the security doc.
[08:53] Owen: Ok last couple things — the debugger has a 'request diff' that shows model outputs side-by-side and highlights token-level timing. It's handy for finding unexpected token slowdowns.
[09:05] Jorge: Nice. Can we export a CSV of clustered errors for our postmortems?
[09:09] Owen: Yep export as CSV or JSON, and you can push to an S3 bucket for retention.
[09:15] [brief silence]
[09:20] Amir: From our side next steps — we want a replay run with our payloads and dedicated vs hosted comparison. Also security docs.
[09:26] Maya: Great, we'll do that. Owen will own the replay run. I'll send security pack.
[09:31] Hana: Also need a pilot checklist for networking — firewall rules, subnets, peering.
[09:36] Maya: We'll include the VPC checklist. For peering we support AWS VPC peering and privateLink, we'll include options.
[09:44] Owen: Quick note on observability — we provide token-level cost breakdown per route so you can map expensive calls to product features.
[09:53] Jorge: Important for us to allocate cost back to business units.
[09:56] Amir: Anything about legal — retention + e-discovery?
[10:00] Maya: We'll include the retention table and e-discovery flow in the security pack.
[10:05] [transition noise]
[10:10] Owen: Ok wrapping up, I'll schedule the replay and share a perf spreadsheet. Any final Qs?
[10:16] Hana: One small thing — will the replay show per-token latencies for each model call?
[10:20] Owen: Yes, per-token timing is available in the debug view if token visibility is enabled.
[10:25] Jorge: Sounds good.
[10:27] Amir: Thanks everyone.
[10:30] Maya: Thanks all, we'll send notes and next steps.
